title: A Quantum Mechanical Approach to the Computation of Rovibrational Spectra of Diatomic Molecules in Strong Magnetic Fields
authors: Nikhil Yenugu, Ashwani K Tiwari, Sangita Sen
abstract: In the absence of experimental data for molecular spectra in strong magnetic fields, high resolution and reliable computational spectra are required for the interpretation of spectra collected from highly magnetic astrophysical objects. In this paper, we extend the Wilson-Hamiltonian framework, recently implemented and benchmarked by us (\textit{J. Chem. Theory Comput.}, \textbf{21}, 9753 (2025) ), to a general three-dimensional framework suitable for computing the rovibrational spectra of diatomic molecules in strong uniform magnetic fields. The field-dependent electronic and nuclear Hamiltonians capture full non-perturbative coupling between particle motion and the field making the method applicable to all field strengths. The electric quadrupole transition moment integrals for rovibrational transitions in external static magnetic fields are formulated, implemented, and computed to yield spectra which respect the selection rules of the molecule-field system. The spectral changes with increasing field strength such as shifting, splitting, merging, appearance and disappearance of peaks are noted. Contributions from electrons and nuclei are studied individually, as well as in unison to reveal the underlying physics such as stiffening of the bond, emergence of a rotational barrier, field-induced coupling/decoupling of states, and symmetry-breaking in rotational and vibrational states. These results provide the first fully quantum mechanical computational results for the rovibrational signature of $^1\mathrm{H}_{2}$ in extreme magnetic field environments with accuracy suitable for experimental interpretation. The methodology developed herein has direct relevance for high-field spectroscopy and astrochemical modeling, both for providing computational data as well as for understanding the spectral impact of strong magnetic fields on electronic structure and nuclear motion in molecules.
summary: This paper develops a fully quantum mechanical method to compute the rovibrational spectra of diatomic molecules in intense magnetic fields. By extending the Wilson-Hamiltonian formalism, the authors accurately model the non-perturbative coupling between molecular motion and the external field. The results provide crucial computational benchmarks for interpreting spectroscopic data from highly magnetized astrophysical environments.
main_problem: The primary challenge is obtaining high-resolution, reliable computational spectra for molecular rovibrational transitions in strong magnetic fields where experimental data are scarce.
main_result: The authors provide the first fully quantum mechanical computation of the $	ext{H}_2$ rovibrational signature in extreme magnetic fields, revealing complex spectral changes like shifting and splitting.
method: They extend the Wilson-Hamiltonian framework to a general three-dimensional grid representation, allowing for a fully quantum mechanical treatment of nuclear motion coupled non-perturbatively to external static magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The system is diatomic molecules (specifically $	ext{H}_2$) subjected to strong uniform magnetic fields. The method utilizes the full non-relativistic Hamiltonian and extends the Wilson formalism to treat both electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom quantum mechanically.
key_observables: Rovibrational spectra, electric quadrupole transition moment integrals, spectral changes (shifting, splitting, merging), bond stiffening, and rotational barriers.
important_parameters: Strong magnetic fields ($B$), ranging from weak intergalactic fields ($\approx 10^{-18} - 10^{-15}$ T) up to ultra-intense fields ($> 10^{11}$ T).
main_assumptions: The framework is based on the non-relativistic Born-Oppenheimer approximation, and while fully quantum mechanical for nuclei, some advanced effects like Berry curvature terms are noted as areas for future inclusion.
figures_summary: Figure 17 presents computed spectra for the surface of a magnetic white dwarf ($T=12000	ext{K}$), illustrating spectral reorganization under extreme field conditions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the need for quantum methods in strong fields, detailing the extension of the Wilson-Hamiltonian framework to 3D, calculating transition moments, and finally presenting detailed analyses of spectral changes by isolating electronic and nuclear contributions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles molecular structure and dynamics under extreme external fields, a core area of AMO physics that bridges quantum chemistry with astrophysics/high-field spectroscopy.
